results.corrected_title: Judge says he is 'highly likely' to grant Apple an injunction against OpenAI in trade-secrets case
results.corrected_summary: At a hearing on 14 October 2026, US District Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal., San Jose) said he is 'highly likely' to grant Apple a preliminary injunction that would bar former Apple employees from using Apple's proprietary information at OpenAI. Apple sued in July 2026, alleging that OpenAI, io Products and former Apple staff took confidential information about product design, manufacturing, components and the supply chain to build consumer hardware. Davila called Apple's request for a broad forensic inspection a 'huge ask'. Bloomberg reports that OpenAI agreed not to use the alleged trade secrets. OpenAI denies wrongdoing and has accused a former employee who went back to Apple of taking confidential OpenAI files. A day earlier, on 13 October, Davila ordered OpenAI to speed up handing over interview records relating to former Apple employees.
key_facts: Case: Apple v. Liu, No. 5:26-cv-07078, N.D. Cal. (San Jose); Judge Edward Davila
The 14 Oct 2026 hearing was preliminary and no written injunction order has been reported; the suit was filed in July 2026
Named individuals include OpenAI hardware chief Tang Tan, Chang Liu and Alyssa Peng (all former Apple employees); io Products is also a defendant

13 Oct order: OpenAI must turn over materials it has already collected within 5 days and other materials within 14 days, including interview checklists, guides and scripts; depositions of Liu, Peng and Tan were approved
Davila turned down some of Apple's broader requests, including expedited access to OpenAI research on metal finishes and power management; OpenAI's motion to dismiss is still pending
OpenAI denies the claims and says Apple is trying to stop employees from leaving for a competitor
results.issues: The core claims check out. The 'highly likely' remark is a preliminary signal, not a ruling, and no injunction has been issued yet. The lawsuit itself is from July 2026, but the 13 Oct order and the 14 Oct hearing are new developments inside the window. Only Claims Journal and TechCrunch were opened directly. io Products as a defendant and OpenAI's agreement not to use the alleged secrets come from search summaries only (9to5Mac and AppleInsider headlines), not from pages I opened.

results.corrected_title: Google DeepMind safety report finds no significant acceleration of AI R&D, even though AI writes over 75% of its code
results.corrected_summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report, published in mid-October 2026, found 'no significant end-to-end acceleration of AI R&D' and rated the risk from AI-driven AI R&D as 'currently low'. Its internal capability index rose about 0.091 points per month before 1 April 2026 and 0.118 points per month after, a difference the report says is not statistically significant. More than 75% of DeepMind's production code is written by AI, and fully delegated pull requests rose from 7.5% in April to 11.9% in September. Meanwhile, co-founder Sergey Brin said Google is 'starting to get onto that RSI treadmill'.
key_facts: The report rates the risk from AI-driven AI R&D as 'currently low' and finds no significant end-to-end acceleration

Capability index (92 benchmarks) slope: 0.091 to 0.118 points/month before and after 1 Apr 2026, not statistically significant; Google attributes Argon sitting above the trend line to more compute and investment
Over 75% of production code at Google DeepMind is AI-written; fully delegated pull requests rose from 7.5% (Apr) to 11.9% (Sep); about 88% still need human steering or human-written code
Argon solves about half of the internal research engineering tasks, far below the 90% level DeepMind treats as a warning signal
The report also draws on a survey of 12 senior leaders and researchers
Sergey Brin, in a Gemini 4 Argon roundtable: Google is 'starting to get onto that RSI treadmill'
results.issues: I did not open the primary Google DeepMind report, so the figures come from TNW and DigitalToday, and the two agree. The exact publication date is not confirmed. Gemini 4 Argon was announced on 30 Sep 2026 but reportedly became generally available on 13 Oct 2026; the report seems to have come out around then (Decrypt covered it on 15 Oct). 13 Oct is plausible but unconfirmed; the event is within the window either way. Brin's remarks are from a video Google shared around 14 Oct.

results.corrected_title: Simons Foundation, OpenAI and Anthropic launch $15 million initiative to help mathematicians vet AI-generated results
results.corrected_summary: On 15 October 2026 the Simons Foundation announced a $15 million initiative with OpenAI and Anthropic to help mathematicians assess, interpret and set standards for AI-generated mathematical results. OpenAI says it is contributing $5 million. The money will fund workshops, conferences, training and an open call for proposals, and both AI labs will give foundation-supported researchers access to their models and computing resources. The initiative follows a backlash over OpenAI's October announcement of more than 700 AI-written manuscripts, which the Association for Human Mathematics condemned as plagiarism.
key_facts: $15 million in combined funding and resources from the Simons Foundation, Anthropic and OpenAI, announced 15 Oct 2026
OpenAI pledged $5 million; I could not confirm how much Anthropic is contributing
The foundation will manage the money, including an open call for proposals; it will also fund workshops, conferences and training
OpenAI and Anthropic will give foundation-supported researchers access to their models and computing resources
Background: on 6 Oct OpenAI said its model had produced more than 700 manuscripts and almost 400 other results; the Association for Human Mathematics accused OpenAI of plagiarism
results.issues: I could not open the Simons Foundation's own press release; the Citybiz copy returned 403. The facts come from Euronews and from search summaries of other coverage. Anthropic's share has not been confirmed: one report says each partner gave $5M, while others say the release does not break down the shares. The original OpenAI manuscript announcement (6 Oct) falls before the window, but this funding announcement is a genuinely new development inside it.
